body:
*Written by the Stylfixx team · Reviewed by Omar Sharieff, Director, Stylfixx Innovations Pvt. Ltd. · Last updated 10 November 2026*

**Quick answer:** Yes, a bathroom can be renovated without removing the old tiles, as long as they are firmly bonded, level and the bathroom does not leak. New tiles are fixed over the old ones with polymer tile adhesive, and fittings, vanity, lighting and paint are changed at the same time. In Bengaluru in 2026 this usually costs ₹80,000 to ₹1.5 lakh and takes 6–9 days, against ₹1.5 to ₹3.5 lakh and 10–15 days for a full demolition. If the bathroom leaks into the room below or next door, the tiles must come out so the floor can be waterproofed.

## Is your bathroom suitable for a no-demolition renovation?

Check these five things before choosing tile-over-tile:

| Check | Good to go | Needs demolition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tap test | Tiles sound solid when tapped | Many tiles sound hollow or are loose |
| Leaks | No damp patches on adjoining walls or the ceiling below | Damp, peeling paint or stains near the bathroom |
| Floor slope | Water runs to the drain | Water stands in corners |
| Plumbing | Pipes and concealed valves work, no leaks | Old GI pipes, low pressure or hidden leaks |
| Floor height | 8–12 mm rise is acceptable at the door and drain | Door gap already tight, or the floor already higher than the room outside |

If any row falls in the right-hand column, a no-demolition makeover only hides the problem. A leaking bathroom needs the tiles removed, the floor waterproofed and tested, then new tiles laid. Our guide to [which waterproofing is best for a terrace](/blog/which-waterproofing-is-best-for-terrace) explains the same preparation principles.

## Ways to renovate without removing tiles

| Option | What it involves | Typical 2026 cost (Bengaluru) | Time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refresh | Deep cleaning, epoxy regrouting, new taps, shower, mirror, lights and paint | ₹45,000 – ₹90,000 | 3–5 days |
| Tile-over-tile makeover | New floor and wall tiles fixed over old tiles with adhesive, plus new fittings | ₹80,000 – ₹1.5 lakh | 6–9 days |
| Full renovation (for comparison) | Demolition, waterproofing, new plumbing, tiles and sanitaryware | ₹1.5 – ₹3.5 lakh | 10–15 days |

Prices are typical market ranges for a 5 × 7 to 6 × 8 ft bathroom; your exact price is fixed in a written quote after a site visit.

### Epoxy regrouting

Old cement grout turns black, cracks and lets water in behind the tiles. Raking it out and refilling with epoxy grout makes old tiles look much cleaner, resists stains and blocks seepage through the joints. It is the cheapest single upgrade for a bathroom with sound tiles.

### Tile-over-tile

The old glazed tiles are cleaned and roughened, then new tiles are fixed with a polymer tile adhesive, not cement mortar, which does not bond to glazed tiles. Large-format tiles cut grout lines and make a small bathroom look bigger. On the floor, choose matt anti-skid tiles; see [which tiles are best for a bathroom floor](/blog/which-tiles-are-best-for-flooring).

### Fittings and fixtures

Most of the visible change comes from fittings: a new wall-mounted or floor-mounted WC, a vanity with storage, a mixer or thermostatic shower, a glass shower partition, a mirror cabinet and LED lighting. Many of these can be swapped without touching the tiles.

### Tile paint and coatings

Epoxy tile paints can change the colour of wall tiles in dry areas, but they wear in showers and on floors. Treat them as a short-term fix for rentals rather than a renovation.

## What to watch out for

- **Floor height:** tile plus adhesive adds about 8–12 mm. The door may need trimming, and the floor trap level must still let water drain.
- **Drain and slope:** the new floor must keep the slope to the drain. A tiler should re-check it with a level before fixing.
- **Hidden plumbing:** concealed pipes behind old tiles cannot be inspected. If they are 20+ years old, consider replacing them now; later repairs mean breaking the new tiles.
- **Wall thickness:** wall tiles over old tiles add thickness around concealed valves and niches, so trims and extension pieces may be needed.
- **Warranty:** ask what the workmanship warranty covers, especially hollow or loose tiles.

## Indian bathroom renovation ideas that work without demolition

- **Wet and dry zones:** a glass partition or curtain keeps the rest of the floor dry.
- **Wall-hung vanity:** frees floor space and makes cleaning easier.
- **Large-format wall tiles** in a light colour, with fewer grout lines.
- **Niches and shelves:** a recessed niche needs some wall cutting, but a slim glass or stainless shelf does not.
- **Better ventilation:** an exhaust fan sized for the room reduces damp and mould.
- **Health faucet and hand shower** on a single diverter, the way most Indian households use bathrooms.

## How Stylfixx renovates bathrooms

Stylfixx renovates bathrooms across Bengaluru, from Hennur, Kalyan Nagar and HRBR Layout to Hebbal, Thanisandra and Frazer Town. We tap-test the old tiles, check for damp with a moisture meter and tell you honestly whether tile-over-tile will last or whether the floor needs waterproofing first. title: Bathroom Renovation Without Removing Tiles: What Works and What It Costs
description: Can you renovate a bathroom without removing tiles? When tile-over-tile works, what it costs in Bangalore in 2026, and when you must demolish instead.

faqs.question: Can new tiles be laid over old bathroom tiles?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the old tiles are firmly bonded, level and the bathroom doesn't leak. The old glaze is cleaned and roughened and the new tiles are fixed with polymer tile adhesive, not cement mortar.

faqs.question: How long does a tile-over-tile bathroom renovation take?
faqs.answer: A tile-over-tile makeover with new fittings usually takes 6 to 9 days, against 10 to 15 days for a full renovation with demolition and waterproofing.

faqs.question: Does tile-over-tile fix a leaking bathroom?
faqs.answer: No. Tiles are not the waterproof layer. If the bathroom leaks into the room below or next door, the tiles must be removed, the floor waterproofed and flood-tested, and new tiles laid.

faqs.question: Will the bathroom floor become higher?
faqs.answer: Yes, by about 8 to 12 mm for tile plus adhesive. The door may need trimming, and the slope to the floor drain must be checked before fixing.

faqs.question: Can I paint bathroom tiles instead?
faqs.answer: Epoxy tile paint can refresh wall tiles in dry areas, but it wears in showers and on floors. Treat it as a short-term fix rather than a renovation.
